method: Both reviewers read every German string of the current file again: title and title.canDo, spec.situation and spec.deviation, the Folge (8 lines, gist item), the LS1 and LS2 dialogues (10 lines each), the LS3 chat, the 5 exam texts (10 ads), the strategy card, every promptDe, option, tile, accepted form and explanation.de, the three micro-outputs, both aussprache blocks (focus, perception pairs, read-aloud lines), the Sp2 and Sp3 parts (instructions, situations, cards, aiRole, openingLine, 8 hintWords, 16 model turns), the S2 task (situation, taskDe, 3 Leitpunkte with cues, checklist, model text), 8 Redemittel with their function labels, the check line, every endLine, story beat and cliffhanger, the rule cards rc.akkusativ and rc.kein (and rc.negation-nicht, which rc.kein now contradicts), and the five registry texts of start.lernziele as the player shows them (compiler.mjs canDoTexts l. 474 → StartView.jsx goals box, CheckView.jsx „Das kann ich“). We solved all authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line, never from promptEn or the key: Folge gist 1, inputItems 3 × 5, structuredInput 3 × 4, pool 11 + 11 + 12, reserve 4 + 5 + 5, LS3 perception 4, L2 5, Check 8, proof 1 (94). Every sentence_building item was permuted against its frame (Aussagesatz, Ja/Nein-Frage, W-Frage), and every error_correction was solved for every correct correction under its now-named category. We ran 33 candidate answers through the real grader, src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js (see validator.grader). Exam blocks were checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json: l2 (5 items, options a/b, per-ad band 9–26 from samples of 11–23 words; recounted with lib-validate wordCount: 12/11, 11/11, 12/11, 12/11, 11/11), sp2 (2 topics, cards-ask), sp3 (2 rounds, cards-request, an information question is sent back), s2 (3 Leitpunkte, about 30 words, Anrede/Gruß not a Leitpunkt; model text 30 words by EXM-03's count). For the lexical and grammar surface we wrote a walker on the validator's own machinery (lexicon.mjs knownForms + licensedForms at a1.1-u06, metalanguage.mjs, compounds.mjs, detectors.mjs detectInText with the full lexicon env, spine.mjs detectorPlacement) and ran it over every German string of the unit, including the surfaces LEX-01 and GRM-04 do not read (perception pairs, cards, hintWords, model turns, Redemittel functions, persona, cliffhanger), over the five can-do registry texts at every a1.1 unit's position, and over every German fix wording proposed below. Lexicon roles were read from a1.1/lexicon.json (promotions []), the spine from grammar-spine.json, can-do modes from registries/cando/a1.json, level limits from level-profiles.json (a1.1: maxWords 12, subordinateClausesMax 0, examStemChars 15–90, ruleCardMaxWords 60). Cast and story were checked against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json (Emre: online from İzmir, works in an Elektrogeschäft; Arjun: Softwareentwickler; Bilal: Informatiker), the u05 cliffhanger (the missing Heft), u01 castIn (Emre enters there), u07 (Folge and LS1: the evening video chat, Emre's shop sells laptops) and the series beat a1.1-u12 → a1.2-u01 (Priya's hotel internship). Every r1 finding was re-checked at its path; every finding class of the u04 trail r1–r5 and of u05 r1 was checked for recurrence.

verdict: Not exit-ready, but the unit's own work is nearly done: 0 BLOCKER, 1 MAJOR, 7 MINOR. All three r1 blockers and all three r1 majors are closed, and the validator is green (ITM-01, LEX-01 and GRM-05 all pass). Every error correction names what to correct. The mein/kein cues now sit on nouns with a distinct plural. Bilal's line is no longer put into Herr Richter's mouth. The missing-word can-do is performed: the learner holds a picture card with no word and has to say „Das ist für mein Handy. Wie heißt das auf Deutsch?“. We solved all 94 items blind and every key is right. Every sentence-building order the frame allows is accepted. The L2 block is now a real paraphrase set of 11–12-word ads, and a word-matching baseline fails three of its five items. Sp2, Sp3 and S2 are exact to sd1.json, and all tasks are original. du/Sie is right in every relationship. The German is correct on every model surface. The one MAJOR is not the unit author's to fix (F01). The Start screen shows the unit's five registry can-do texts German-only, directly under the title.canDo that r1-F02 cleaned. Those texts carry ob-, dass- and wenn-clauses, a zu-infinitive, the Perfekt and „kurze Nachricht mit passender Anrede“. No rail reads them. The same holds in 53 of the 56 Lernziele texts of a1.1, so this is a gate hole and stop-the-line for the level. The minors: ls3-mo repeats r1-F16's colon shape and ls1-mo relies on a word from LS2 (F02). The new ls2-i01 gives away two later items (F03). Bilal knows about a request he did not hear and searches before the evening he announced (F04). The unit's main contrast, nicht vs kein, has no error tag, so two items point at the wrong repair card (F05). Three findings are carried from r1 and held by owners: the rule cards and spine (F06), the lexicon roles (F07). Finally, r1-F15's lp2 now overlaps lp1 (F08).

findings.problem: r1-F02 rewrote title.canDo to take out „kurze“ and „passender“, because LEX-01 walks that line and failed it hard. The player puts the unit's five registry can-do texts on the same Start screen, one card lower. They appear German-only, unglossed, with no English twin, and the Check screen repeats them under „Das kann ich“. At a1.1-u06 every one of the five carries a construction from A2.1 to B1.1, or a word from a later unit. cd.a1.nachricht-anrede carries the exact phrase r1-F02 removed. The a1.1 profile allows no subordinate clause, and four of the five texts have one. A learner at unit 6 meets three subordinate clause types, a zu-infinitive and a Perfekt on the screen that is supposed to tell them what they will learn. No rail sees this. walkReadSurfaces yields title.canDo but not the Lernziele texts, so a class that is a blocker on one line passes unseen on the next card. Under §9.4 that is a gate hole, which is MAJOR. We ran the walker at every unit's own position and left out the „Ich kann“ frame (g.koennen, u08). By that count, 53 of the 56 Lernziele texts of a1.1 u01–u12 carry a look-ahead, and every unit is affected. The class is therefore stop-the-line for the level. The unit author cannot fix any of this, because the unit carries only the ids.
